title: Pose Matcher: a new desktop interface
question: Choose the interface to build. Both directions keep the camera, pose guidance, and reaction together.

options.label: Camera workspace
options.lineage: Compact digital-camera displays and desktop camera controls
options.thesis: A generous viewfinder beside a precise, quiet reaction panel.
options.viewport: Camera takes two thirds of the window; the right panel holds pose instructions and the match; camera and overlay controls sit below.
options.risk: Quiet precision depends on excellent spacing and real controls, not decorative camera chrome.

raised.raise: Every control says exactly what it does.
State changes must remain legible across the whole camera session.
Controls get generous targets and plain-language empty states.
Live measurements have stable positions and never move neighboring controls.
A matched pose earns one immediate, unmistakable reaction reveal.

options.label: Desk controller
options.thesis: The camera becomes a desktop instrument with distinct physical-looking control keys.
options.viewport: A wide camera and reaction monitor sit above grouped camera, overlay, and exit keys.
options.case: Strong control clarity; less familiar to casual users than a camera workspace.
options.risk: Tactile controls can compete with the camera if the hardware metaphor gets too heavy.

options.label: Industrial labels
options.thesis: Camera zones marked like equipment labels.
options.viewport: Large labeled camera and reaction zones.
options.case: The labels distract from the playful content and add reading work.
options.risk: Heavy labels can dominate the subject.

options.label: Deep dive
options.thesis: A depth-like sequence guides each pose.
options.viewport: Camera alongside a vertical pose progression.
options.case: A staged journey misrepresents two gestures that are always available.
options.risk: Unrelated underwater language obscures the task.

options.label: Soft consumer app
options.thesis: A friendly stack of camera and pose cards.
options.viewport: Camera and reactions stacked over a bottom toolbar.
options.case: The scrolling card stack weakens simultaneous camera and reaction viewing.
options.kept: Generous targets and understandable empty states.
options.risk: The generic card treatment could repeat the look you want to leave behind.

options.label: Laboratory counter
options.thesis: Pose detection presented through large numeric readouts.
options.viewport: Readouts above smaller camera and image panels.
options.case: Numbers are secondary to the human pose and reaction image.
options.risk: A technical measurement tool overwhelms a casual activity.

options.label: Arcade screen
options.thesis: Pose matching becomes a pixel-grid playfield.
options.viewport: Camera framed by game-style pose indicators.
options.case: Retro pixels conflict with the requested modern GUI and reduce video clarity.
options.risk: The retro effect could overpower the real images.

canonCard.label: Standard desktop app
canonCard.thesis: A conventional camera application with familiar native controls.
canonCard.viewport: A camera pane, a reaction sidebar, and a conventional toolbar.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and useful, with little distinct identity.
